transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. ____. Um, it's really nice to meet you. Thank you for fitting me in. 

I, uh... I guess I'm here because things have been a little stressful at my job. I'm a buyer, and... well, I really hope this doesn't make me sound difficult or anything. I know I probably shouldn't be thinking this way. But lately, I just can't shake this feeling that people at work, and even some of our vendors, are tracking my buys behind my back. Like they're intentionally messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. 

I know how that sounds, I really do. My supervisor actually sat me down and showed me the reports to prove that nothing like that is happening. And I really want to agree with her, you know, so I'm doing a good job and not causing trouble, but I just... I still feel like it's happening, even with the reports. 

Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I started with that.
When your supervisor showed you the reports, did that change your belief at all?

I mean, I really tried to let it change my mind. I sat there with her, and I nodded, and I looked at all the spreadsheets she printed out. I wanted to just agree and be a good employee, you know? But... no, it didn't really change anything. 

Even looking right at the numbers, I just kept thinking that they could have been altered before she printed them, or that the vendors are keeping a separate set of books just to mess with my launches. I know it sounds terrible to say that about my coworkers. I really don't want to be the kind of person who thinks everyone is out to get them. But I just can't shake the feeling, no matter what proof she shows me. 

Is it bad that I still feel that way, even after she tried to help? I just want to be doing a good job.
Do you believe anyone else outside of work is also trying to track you or interfere with your life?

No, no, definitely not. Um, it's really just at work. I mean, my friends and my family, they're all great. I wouldn't want you to think I'm, like, completely paranoid about everyone in my life, because I'm really not. 

Outside of the office, everything is totally fine. I don't feel like anyone is following me or, you know, trying to mess with me in my personal life. It's really just tied to my job and those specific vendors. 

I hope that's a good thing, right? That it's just contained to work? I'm really trying to keep things normal everywhere else.
When these worries about your coworkers started, did you ever notice any changes in your mood, like feeling unusually down or unusually high?

Um, well... I guess there have been some changes, maybe? I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm all over the place, because I really do try to keep things steady. But, um... yeah, sometimes I get these stretches where I just feel... really, really good. Like, almost too good? Like the whole city is just opening up for me and I can do anything. 

It's actually kind of a nice feeling, to be honest. But... well, the downside is that during those times, if someone at work questions a purchase order or tells me I need to slow down, I... I can get a little short with them. Like, I snap way harder than I mean to. 

I always feel terrible about it afterward. I really try to be a team player and keep everyone happy. I don't want them to think I'm hard to work with. Is it normal to get a little irritable like that when you're feeling really energetic? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Have you always tended to be suspicious of other people, even before these work problems started?

No, definitely not. I mean, I've always been a pretty trusting guy, you know? I like to think the best of people. I really do. 

Um, it's just been recently that I've felt this way. Well, I guess... I guess it's been going on for about ten months now? That's when I started getting really worried about the vendors, and... and when I started hearing that voice I mentioned before. 

I know ten months sounds like a long time to be dealing with this, and I probably should have said something sooner. I just kept hoping it would go away if I worked hard enough and stayed positive. I really didn't want to be a bother to anyone. Do you think it's okay that I waited this long to get help? I really am trying my best to handle it all.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days or longer when you felt abnormally energized or unusually happy and needed much less sleep than usual?

Um, well... yeah, I guess that does happen sometimes. I hope you don't think I'm neglecting my health or anything, because I really do try to take care of myself. But... yeah, there have been plenty of weeks where I sleep maybe, like, three or four hours a night. 

The thing is, I don't feel tired at all when it happens. I actually wake up feeling totally wired and ready to go. I just get this mindset that lying in bed is just wasting time, you know? Like, it's time I could use to make moves and get things done. 

I mean, being driven and having all that energy is a good thing, right? I just really want to be productive and do a good job for my team. I figure as long as I'm getting my work done, it's okay to not sleep as much... is that alright?
During those times when you sleep very little, do you feel unusually happy or irritable for most of the day?

Um, well... yeah, I guess I do. I think I mentioned it a little bit earlier, but, um... yeah, during those weeks when I'm not sleeping much, I get those stretches where I just feel... really, really amazing. Like the whole city is just opening up for me, you know? It's a really great feeling, and I feel so capable. 

But... well, I guess the other side of it is that... yeah, I can get a little irritable, too. Like I said before, if I'm feeling that good and working that fast, and then someone at work questions a purchase order or tells me I need to slow down... I just snap at them. Way harder than I mean to. 

I really hate that I do that. I try so hard to be polite and professional with everyone, I promise I do. It just sort of slips out when I'm feeling that energized. Do you think that makes me a bad coworker? I really don't want people to think I'm mean or anything.
During those times when you feel unusually energized and need much less sleep, do you also become more active or driven to start lots of projects or take on more than usual?

Um, yeah... I do tend to take on a lot when I'm feeling like that. I mean, I really just want to be as helpful as possible to the company, you know? I want to show them I'm a hard worker. 

So when I get all keyed up, it's like... I can't just handle one task at a time. I'll be emailing three different vendors at once, drafting up a new buy plan, reorganizing all the product samples in the back... and I just kind of pace around the office while I'm doing it. It's like if I stop moving, I'll lose my train of thought, or lose that momentum. 

I know it probably looks a little chaotic to the people around me, and I really don't want to stress anyone out. I just get so focused on getting everything done perfectly. Is it okay to work like that sometimes? I mean, multitasking is a good skill to have in retail, right? I just hope I'm not overstepping or doing things wrong.
When you hear the voice, does it happen only during the times when you’re feeling unusually energized or unusually down?

Um, well... I hope it doesn't sound like I'm completely losing my grip or anything, but... no, it's not just when I'm feeling all keyed up or really low. 

There was this one time, maybe a few months ago, where I was actually feeling pretty level. I was sleeping a normal amount, not feeling like I had to run the whole market or anything like that. Just... calm, I guess. But even then, for a few weeks, I still had this really strong feeling that people were tracking my buys. And... um, I still heard the voice when I was alone in the stockroom. 

I know that probably sounds bad, and I really tried to just ignore it and focus on my work. I didn't want to make a big deal out of it or worry anyone. Is it... is it really unusual that it happens even when I'm feeling okay otherwise? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so I can get better.
Have you had any periods of at least two weeks when you were not having manic or depressive symptoms, but you were still hearing the voice or believing people at work were tracking you?

Um, yeah... I think I just mentioned it, but yes. I hope it's okay that I'm repeating myself, I just want to be sure I'm answering you right. 

But, um, yes, there was that time a few months ago. It was a calmer stretch, you know? I was sleeping normally, I wasn't feeling super down, and I wasn't all wound up feeling like I was running the whole market either. I was just... fine. But even then, for like, I don't know, a few weeks... I still really believed people were tracking my buys. And I still heard that voice when I was in the stockroom. 

I really tried to push it out of my head, I promise. I didn't let it affect my work or anything. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the details you need.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest or pleasure in things most of the day, nearly every day?

Um, depressed? I mean, I don't really think so. Not like, not for two whole weeks or anything where I couldn't do things. 

I mean, everyone gets a little stressed or tired sometimes, right? Especially in retail, the hours can be kind of long, and you just want to go home and rest. But I always make sure I get to work and do my job well. I wouldn't want to let my team down by just, you know, moping around or losing interest in my work. 

I try to stay really positive, honestly. So, um, no, I don't think I've ever had a time like that where I felt down all day every day. Is it... is it a good thing that I haven't? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay.

Have there been any times when the voice or the belief that people at work were tracking you continued while you were feeling completely back to normal and not having any manic or depressive symptoms?

Um, yes, actually. I know we just talked about it, and I'm sorry if I'm sounding like a broken record, I really don't mean to waste your time. But yes, that time a few months ago... I was feeling completely normal. Not too high, not down at all. I was sleeping fine, and I definitely didn't feel like I was running the whole market or anything crazy like that. 

But even though I was feeling totally fine, for a few weeks, I still had that... that feeling that people were tracking my buys. And I still heard the voice when I was alone in the stockroom. 

I feel a little silly bringing it up again, but I just want to make absolutely sure I'm answering your questions right so you have everything you need. I really was trying my best to just ignore it and do my job. Is it helpful that I'm telling you this again? I hope I'm being a good patient.
Have you ever had a period of at least one week when your mood was so elevated or irritable and your energy was so high that other people could clearly tell you were not yourself?

Um, well... I mean, I guess there have been times where I felt really, really good. Like, super energetic, you know? But it's a good thing, right? To have a lot of energy for work? 

I do get these stretches where I just feel like... like the whole city is opening up for me, and I can just tackle anything that comes my way. I get so much done. But, um... sometimes if someone questions a purchase order I made, or if my manager tells me to slow down, I might... well, I might snap a little. Way harder than I mean to, honestly. 

I always feel really bad about it after. I don't want to be difficult to work with, and I always apologize. Do you think that's what you mean? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples. I really try to keep my cool most of the time.
Have the voice and the belief that coworkers were tracking you ever appeared only when you were having those high-energy, little-sleep periods?

Um, well, yes... they did happen together sometimes. Like, when I had those really high-energy weeks where I barely slept at all and just talked constantly about all the new sneaker trends... I felt amazing, like I was totally untouchable at work. 

And during those exact same times, I also felt really sure that the vendors were, you know, manipulating the numbers behind my back. And that voice would be there too, just pushing me to move faster and faster. 

So they definitely happened at the same time, but... but like I said before, I also had the voice and the tracking thing when I was feeling totally normal, too. I hope it's okay that I'm explaining it this way. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture so you know I'm trying my best to be helpful.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest or pleasure in things nearly every day?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I have days where I'm maybe a little tired or just not super excited to go into the stockroom, but I wouldn't call it depressed. I always try to keep a positive attitude, you know? 

I definitely haven't had anything like that last for two whole weeks. I try really hard to stay on top of my game at work, and I wouldn't want to let a bad mood get in the way of that. I always try to find the bright side of things. 

Does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm not, like, missing something you're looking for. But yeah, I generally try to stay pretty upbeat.
Have you ever had a period of at least one week when you felt so unusually energized or irritable that other people could clearly tell you were not yourself?

Um, well... I guess when I get really keyed up like that, I do try to channel it into being super productive, you know? Like, I'll be emailing three different vendors at the same time, putting together a whole new buy plan, and reorganizing all the floor samples. 

I just... I feel like if I stop moving, I'll lose the thread of what I'm doing. So I end up pacing around the office a lot while I work. I know it probably looks a little intense to other people, but I really just want to make sure I'm getting everything done perfectly.

Have you ever had a period when you felt so unusually energized or irritable that other people clearly noticed you were not yourself?

Well, yeah, I guess so. I mean, I have these stretches where... where it feels like the whole city is just opening up for me, you know? Like I can see all the possibilities for the store and I'm just so dialed in. It feels really good, honestly.

I might snap at them. Way harder than I mean to, really. I always feel bad about it after, because I want to be easy to work with. I'm usually a really relaxed guy! 

I just get so focused on doing a great job that I get a little impatient. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a difficult person to be around. I really do try to keep things friendly at work.
Have you ever had a stretch of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or believing people at work were tracking you, but you were not having any manic symptoms at all?

Um, yeah, I guess so. There was a time, actually... well, I was definitely sleeping a lot better. I was getting my full eight hours, and I didn't have that feeling like I had to run the whole market all by myself. I felt pretty calm, honestly. 

But even then, for a couple of weeks, I still had this really strong feeling that people were tracking my buys. And... and I was still hearing that voice when I was alone in the stockroom. 

I know that probably sounds a little strange, and I really hope you don't think I'm crazy or anything. I just want to be totally honest with you so you can help me. Does that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you ever had any delusions or hallucinations for at least two weeks when you were not having any manic or depressive symptoms?

Um, yes, I think we just talked about that a little bit, but to make sure I'm answering you right... yeah, there was definitely a time when I wasn't feeling all sped up or super down either. 

Like I said, I was sleeping a lot more normally, and I didn't feel that intense pressure like I had to run the whole market myself. I was feeling pretty even, honestly. But even during that calmer stretch, for a few weeks, I still really believed people were tracking my buys. And I was still hearing that voice when I'd go back into the stockroom. 

I really hope that's helpful for you to know. I know it sounds a little weird that it was still happening even when I felt okay otherwise. Am I explaining that clearly enough? I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient and giving you what you need.

When you’re having the voice or the belief that people are tracking you, do you ever have times when those symptoms seem especially tied to your high-energy or low mood periods, or do they usually happen on their own?

Um, yeah, they definitely overlap sometimes. Like... well, I remember those weeks when I was feeling really, really energized? I was barely sleeping at all, but I felt, I don't know, just untouchable at work. I was talking nonstop about sneaker trends to anyone who would listen. I probably got a little carried away, honestly, but I just get so passionate about doing a good job. I hope that doesn't make me sound too intense or anything. 

But, um... during that same time, when I was all sped up like that, that's when I was also really convinced the vendors were manipulating the numbers on me. And I'd hear that voice, too, just... pushing me to move faster. 

So, yeah, they do happen at the same time sometimes. I hope I'm explaining that right? I just want to be as helpful as I can be for you.
